tools.name: account_status
tools.description: Report this account's plan and usage live: whether hosted audits are active, the page budget used and remaining in the rolling 30 days and when it resets, how long crawl sessions are kept, and the licenses on the account. Call it when a tool returned trial_expired, no_hosted_addon or quota_exceeded,

tools.name: check_page
tools.description: Audit one URL immediately and return its SEO issues (schema bseoa.issue/v1: key, category, severity, message, fix_hint, docs_url). This is the fast path and the right first call for "what is wrong with this page?" - it fetches a single page and never follows links. Prefer it over start_crawl wheneve

tools.name: compare_crawls
tools.description: Compare two crawls of the same site and report which issues are new in the later crawl, which were fixed, and how many persist. Use it to answer "did my changes help?" or "what regressed since the last deploy?", and to gate a release: only the new_issues list represents a regression, so a pre-existi

tools.name: crawl_status
tools.description: Report the progress of a crawl started by start_crawl: state ("queued", "running", "finished" or "failed"), the crawl session_id to read results from, the pages stored so far, and the error text if it failed. Poll every few seconds; a queued crawl starts as soon as the worker is free. Do not call is

tools.name: issues_summary
tools.description: Summarize a crawl: total issue count, counts by severity and by category, and every distinct issue key with how many pages it affects plus up to five example URLs. Always call this before query_issues - it is small, it tells you which keys are worth drilling into, and it is what you should base a pr

tools.name: list_crawls
tools.description: List the crawl sessions stored for this account, newest last, with their session_id, start URL, start and end times, and page count. Single-page checks made with check_page are not crawls and are not listed. Call this first when the user refers to "the last crawl" or when you need a session_id for i

tools.name: page_report
tools.description: Report everything recorded about one crawled URL: status code, redirect target, title and meta description, Open Graph tags, word count, link and asset counts, headings, TTFB, Web Vitals score, and the full issue list for that page. Use it after query_issues or issues_summary when you need the conte

tools.name: query_issues
tools.description: List individual issues from a crawl, filtered by severity, issue key, category or URL prefix, as bseoa.issue/v1 records with the affected URL, the localized message, a fix hint and a docs link. Returns at most 100 issues per call: when the response has a non-null next_offset there are more, so call

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search Black SEO Analyzer's own documentation and return the matching sections with their URLs. Use it for questions about bseoa itself: what a tool, command, flag or setting does, crawl limits and the page budget, licenses and the hosted plan, installing or configuring the CLI, GUI or connector, or

tools.name: serp_preview
tools.description: Fetch each URL and report how its title and meta description will look in a search result: character length, pixel width, whether the engine will truncate it, and the Open Graph and Twitter Card fallbacks. Use it when the user asks how a page "looks in Google" or is rewriting titles and descriptions

tools.name: start_crawl
tools.description: Queue a crawl of a whole site and return a job_id immediately; a worker runs the crawl and the pages count against the account's rolling 30-day page budget. Use it only when the user asks to crawl or audit a site, or names a number of pages; a request to check a single URL, even a homepage, is check

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "check_page" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.
